questions.q: What language are Cosmos DB stored procedures, triggers, and UDFs written in?
options: JavaScript, executed inside the database engine itself
T-SQL, identical to SQL Server
PL/SQL, like Oracle
Python
questions.explain: Cosmos DB's server-side programming model uses JavaScript functions registered against a container, not a proprietary procedural SQL dialect.

questions.q: What is the real constraint on a Cosmos DB stored procedure's transactional guarantee?
options: It only covers a single logical partition — there is no cross-partition transaction
It covers the entire database account across all containers
Stored procedures in Cosmos DB have no transactional guarantee at all
The transaction boundary is the entire container, regardless of partition
questions.explain: Multi-statement atomicity in a Cosmos DB stored procedure only holds within a single logical partition key.

questions.q: Why won't a Cosmos DB post-trigger fire automatically on every insert, unlike a SQL Server AFTER INSERT trigger?
options: A pre-trigger or post-trigger must be explicitly named on the create/replace/delete request that invokes it — nothing fires automatically
Cosmos DB triggers always fire automatically, identical to SQL Server
Post-triggers don't exist in Cosmos DB
Triggers only work with the MongoDB API, not the Core API
questions.explain: The client must opt in by explicitly naming the trigger on each request — there's no automatic firing behavior.

questions.q: How is a Cosmos DB UDF called inside a query?
options: With a udf. prefix, e.g. udf.toFahrenheit(c.tempCelsius)
UDFs cannot be called from within a query
By wrapping the query in a stored procedure
Using the EXEC keyword like a T-SQL stored procedure
questions.explain: A UDF is called with the udf. prefix, playing the same role as a T-SQL scalar function used inline in a SELECT list.

questions.q: What is the real distinction between a pre-trigger and a post-trigger in Cosmos DB?
options: A pre-trigger runs before the operation (validate/modify the incoming document); a post-trigger runs after (update related documents or write an audit record)
Pre-triggers only work on reads; post-triggers only work on writes
There is no real difference between them
Pre-triggers are written in JavaScript, post-triggers are written in SQL
questions.explain: Pre-triggers act before the create/replace/delete completes; post-triggers act after it, both only when explicitly named on the request.
